ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: AML/CFT: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism as amended, implemented by the Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Financing of Terrorism Unit (AMLCFT) and Central Bank of Egypt sectoral instructions. UBO register: Unified Companies Law No. 194 of 2020 and its Executive Regulations, requiring every Egyptian limited liability company to maintain and file with GAFI an ultimate beneficial owner register identifying any individual holding or controlling more than 25% of shares, voting rights, or equivalent ownership interest.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified public extract or certificate of incumbency of any non-Egyptian corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or registrar of the jurisdiction of incorporation of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization only; Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, therefore the document must be notarized in the issuing jurisdiction, attested by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and legalized by the competent Egyptian Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Egyptian incorporation agent and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the jurisdiction of execution, countersigned by an Egyptian Consulate when executed outside Egypt
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization by the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate with jurisdiction over the place of execution; if executed in Egypt, authentication by an Egyptian Notary Public attached to the Ministry of Justice

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the bio-data page of the passport of every Ultimate Beneficial Owner and every authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport and national identity issuance authority of the person's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized true copy followed by Consular Legalization at the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate covering the issuing country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds certificate for the share capital contribution and proposed project financing payments
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank of the foreign shareholder, plus confirmation from an Egyptian licensed bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authenticated by the issuing bank's authorized officer, then notarized and consular-legalized as required by the receiving Egyptian bank or AMLCFT expectations

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of every UBO, director, manager, and authorized signatory against: (i) the Egyptian AMLCFT terrorist list and official gazette sanctions list; (ii) the UN Security Council consolidated list and UN sanctions resolutions; (iii) OFAC SDN and other US consolidated sanctions lists; (iv) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list; (v) UK OFSI consolidated list; and (vi) relevant national and international databases of adverse media and criminal enforcement. Persons identified as Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates are subject to Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD), including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification. PEP status must be reassessed continuously, and all screening data must be retained in the client KYC file for at least five years after the termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Egypt Investor Services Portal and GAFI Unified Company Registration System (www.gafi.gov.eg; electronic name clearance available through the Invest in Egypt portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The commercial name of an Egyptian LLC must be composed in Arabic and is filed in Arabic as the controlling legal name. A Latin/English transliteration may be registered as an auxiliary trade name where required for foreign commerce, subject to prior GAFI approval. The name must be unique, not misleading, consistent with the licensed activity, and must not imitate any existing registered domestic or protected foreign company name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If GAFI rejects a proposed name, the applicant may request a reconsideration before the GAFI Investor Services Committee within 15 working days of the rejection notice, submitting the written rejection reason and up to five revised alternative names. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an administrative appeal before the Egyptian Council of State (State Council) under the Administrative Judiciary Law within 60 days of notification. No rejected name may be reused while an appeal is pending or after final administrative rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not acceptable as the sole registered office for an LLC engaged in heavy tunnel boring machine spare parts manufacturing or trading. Egyptian company and commercial registry law requires a physical address in Egypt where corporate records, books, seals, and official notices are maintained. A virtual or serviced correspondence address may be used only as a supplementary mailing/representative address and cannot replace on-site registered substance. Industrial operations must have a separate licensed industrial premises under the Industrial Development Authority requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High. For this industrial sector, the estimated probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first operational year is 70–80%, due to mandatory supervision by the Industrial Development Authority, GAFI, the Egyptian Tax Authority, the Social Insurance Authority, and the General Security apparatus. An actual physical registered office with original statutory records must therefore be available on site at all times.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018 and Executive Regulations No. 96 of 1982; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Law No. 95 of 2015 on Industrial Development; Law No. 4 of 1994 on Environment, as amended
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Investor Services Center and Commercial Registry Department, Cairo One-Stop-Shop
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Association (Aqd Al-Ta'sis) together with the commercial registration application form and the Commercial Register Extract (Qayd Al-Tijari)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed for a standard LLC engaged in manufacturing; the cash subscription declared in the Articles of Association must be deposited into a bank formation account prior to registration. Legal escrow is not required, but funds are blocked until the Commercial Registry Extract is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [EG_LLC] - adopted at [Cairo] on [date], by the founding shareholders acting as interim board. RESOLVED: (1) The share capital as stated in the Articles of Association be subscribed and allotted to the shareholders named therein. (2) The registered office of the Company be fixed and established at [address], Cairo, Egypt, and that address be recorded for all statutory notices and service of process. (3) [Name] be appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] Company Secretary, each with authority to open bank accounts, complete company registration, execute documents, and obtain industrial licenses. (4) All officers are directed to comply with tax, environmental, and civil defense requirements, and perform every act incidental to full incorporation and commencement of business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Registration Name Reservation and Activity Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Investor Services Center / GAFI Digital Submission Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online name reservation application submitting at least three proposed Arabic or transliterated names, state the precise industrial activity as ISIC 2824 - manufacture of underground tunnel boring machines and rotary cutters, and pay the prescribed fee. Obtain the GAFI name clearance certificate. No notarization is required at this stage.
required_dossiers: Signed name reservation application form
Copy of founding shareholders' passports
Draft Articles of Association
Board resolution authorizing formation
Statement of capital contribution and share allocation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected for similarity or inconsistency, submit the alternate proposed names through the same GAFI portal. A formal administrative objection may be filed with the GAFI Legal Affairs Department within 30 days of rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Association and Valuation of In-Kind Contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public Office (Shahr Al-Aqari) in conjunction with GAFI Authenticity Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the Arabic-language Articles of Association identifying shareholders, capital, management structure, and registered office. All founding shareholders must appear before the notary or validly represented by notarized powers of attorney to sign. In-kind contributions, if any, must be supported by a certified independent valuation report attached to the Articles.
required_dossiers: Final draft of Articles of Association
Passport copies of all founding shareholders
Notarized power of attorney if signed by representative
Certified in-kind valuation report, if applicable
Capital subscription schedule and share allocation table
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a deficiency note for missing signatures, incorrect statutory data, or valuation defects, cure the omitted item and resubmit the corrected document for re-notarization. Administrative correction is processed directly with the notary office without court intervention.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Formation Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian Commercial Bank under Central Bank of Egypt supervision
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a formation deposit account in the name of the company under formation at an Egyptian bank. Deposit the subscribed cash capital into that account and obtain a bank capital deposit certificate. The bank will block withdrawals until the Commercial Registry Extract is presented and a licensed officer is registered.
required_dossiers: GAFI name reservation certificate
Notarized Articles of Association
Passport copies of founding shareholders and authorized signatories
Formation board resolution appointing bank account signatories
Company lease or address declaration if requested by bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional corporate existence proof before registering the formation account, provide the GAFI name clearance certificate and notarized Articles. If the deposit certificate is delayed, escalate to the bank's branch manager and, if necessary, submit a complaint to the Central Bank of Egypt for resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Commercial Registry Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration and Commercial Registry Department, Cairo One-Stop-Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation file to GAFI, including the notarized Articles of Association, bank capital deposit certificate, name clearance, and address documentation. Pay the consolidated state registration fee. GAFI verifies statutory compliance, records the company in the Commercial Registry, and issues the official Commercial Register Extract and certificate of incorporation.
required_dossiers: GAFI name reservation certificate
Notarized Articles of Association
Bank capital deposit certificate
Lease contract or registered address proof for the registered office
Formation board resolution
Power of attorney for the submitting agent, if applicable
Receipt of payment of state filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI raises a query on the filing, respond in writing with corrected documents within 10 working days through the GAFI case manager. If rejection is maintained, file an administrative appeal before the GAFI Dispute Resolution Committee within 30 days of the rejection notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Issuance of Tax Card
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) Central and Branch Registration Offices / Electronic Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the Egyptian Tax Authority for a Tax Identification Number and Tax Card after receiving the Commercial Registry Extract. File the prescribed registration forms, declare the activity as heavy machinery manufacturing, and apply for value-added tax registration if annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed the VAT registration threshold. Complete stamp duty filings applicable to the Articles.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register Extract
Notarized Articles of Association
Formation board resolution
Tax registration application form
Address proof for registered and operational premises
Bank capital deposit certificate
Passport copies of officers and board members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA requests economic substance evidence before issuing the Tax Card, submit lease contracts, staffing declarations, physical site photographs, and projected manufacturing documentation. Where the VAT registration is disputed, file an objection with the Egyptian Tax Authority within 30 days of the notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial Operation Licensing and Civil Defense Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Industrial Development (IDA) and the Civil Defense Directorate under the Ministry of Interior
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an industrial establishment license application to IDA for the operational factory premises. Include the production process description for tunnel boring machine spare parts, equipment layout, fire safety design, waste handling, and environmental clearance from the Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency. Arrange the Civil Defense inspection and obtain the fire safety certificate. After all clearances are issued, receive the Industrial Operation License authorizing commencement of manufacturing.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register Extract and Tax Card
Notarized Articles of Association
Industrial license application form prescribed by IDA
Factory lease or land usufruct agreement
Building construction and structural safety certificates
Production process flow and machinery layout description
Environmental Impact Assessment approval from EEAA
Civil Defense fire safety inspection documents
Ministry of Manpower occupational safety and health clearance report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IDA returns the license application for correction, address the inspector comments and resubmit an amended file within 30 days. If the Civil Defense clearance is denied, remedy the fire safety deficiencies and request a re-inspection. Administrative appeal against denial may be filed with the IDA Appeals Committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: General Authority for Industrial Development (IDA), Ministry of Trade and Industry - Industrial Licensing and Compliance Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Operation License (Rekhasa Tashghil) / Factory Operation Permit under Law No. 95 of 2015

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Mandatory Initial Environmental Examination (IEE) report for heavy machinery and metal fabrication. Proponents may be upgraded to a Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) if the facility uses hazardous coatings, large-scale metal finishing, or exceeds facility area thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with EEAA decrial limits under Law No. 4/1994, as amended, including water pollutant discharge standards under EEAA Decree 44/2000; air emission and VOC limits for painting and machining operations; and hazardous waste handling, storage, transportation, and disposal requirements under the Egyptian Waste Management Regulation 2021. Wastewater to public sewer must meet pH, oil and grease, suspended solids, and heavy metal thresholds. Solvent vapors from cleaning and coating operations require local exhaust ventilation and emission controls.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense clearance confirming fire alarm and suppression systems, emergency exits, hazardous material storage safety, and structural fire resistance. A licensed structural engineer certificate is required to verify floor loading for heavy machinery. Ministry of Manpower occupational safety and health clearance is required for cranes, pressure vessels, electrical installations, and worker protective equipment programs.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; e-services portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing platform: https://invoice.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign-owned Egyptian LLC must complete incorporation with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI), then file a tax registration application with the Egyptian Tax Authority using the prescribed Form No. 1. Supporting documents include the notarized certificate of incorporation, commercial registry extract, articles of association, board resolution, accepted signature specimens, power of attorney or tax representative appointment, registered office lease, and identity documents of directors and shareholders. After document review and site verification, the ETA issues a permanent Tax Card (بطاقة ضريبية) containing the corporate tax ID number. The LLC must in parallel register for VAT under Law No. 67 of 2016 if its taxable supplies are expected to exceed the threshold, and also register for employer-related payroll, stamp duties, and any applicable withholding tax obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation_With_Worldwide_Income; the Egyptian LLC is a resident juridical person subject to corporate income tax under Law No. 91 of 2005 on worldwide income. There is no pass-through treatment; profits are taxed at the corporate entity level. Non-resident shareholders receiving dividends are subject to dividend withholding tax at a rate of 10% unless a lower tax treaty rate applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egyptian tax law does not provide check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch pass-through elections for LLCs. Available mechanisms include selection of a non-calendar fiscal year with prior ETA approval, voluntary VAT registration before the mandatory threshold is crossed, election of VAT filing frequency subject to ETA classification, and use of advance pricing agreement and mutual agreement procedure mechanisms for cross-border related-party transactions. No domestic hybrid mismatch election exists; taxpayers must document compliance with BEPS Action 2 principles in cross-border structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended by subsequent rate and relief orders
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of cumulative taxable supplies within any 12 consecutive months; imports are taxable with no registration threshold; non-resident suppliers of cross-border electronic services may become registrable under special attendance rules even below the threshold if supplying final consumers in Egypt.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing applies to all VAT-registered taxpayers, including the subject LLC. Invoices must be prepared in the ETA’s prescribed XML/JSON schema and transmitted in real time through a certified integration. Both seller and buyer must apply for an ETA qualification and obtain a unique multi-purpose digital identification. The ETA’s electronic clearance engine validates the invoice online, rejects non-compliant documents, and returns a unique QR-based authentication code. No legally valid invoice can be issued without real-time clearance. Fiscal data matching with customs declarations and banking records is automated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export sales of tunnel boring machine spare parts qualify for 0% VAT if the registered LLC can prove actual and definitive exportation from Egypt under the Egyptian Customs Law. The goods must be physically shipped outside Egyptian territory, title and risk must pass to the non-resident buyer, and export proceeds must be received in Egypt in a freely convertible currency. Indirect export sales through an Egyptian intermediate supplier are also zero-rated when the final export is documented. The zero-rate applies to the export of goods and certain offshore services listed under the VAT executive regulations.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Certified Customs Export Declaration (Form SAD) endorsed by the Egyptian Customs Authority and showing the TBM spare-part commodity code, quantity, value, and outbound customs office of departure.
Bill of Lading or signed Air Waybill evidencing physical export from Egypt, the exporting party, and the final foreign destination; combined with shipping container/tracking records where applicable.

Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by a bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt confirming receipt of the export proceeds in convertible foreign currency in the exporter’s Egyptian bank account within the statutory period.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA uses the e-invoicing/customs/bank data lake to detect export zero-rating abuse. If any condition is not met within 180 days or the documentation is misstated, the 0% treatment is retrospectively revoked, VAT is assessed at 14% on the gross export value, and a delay penalty of 0.5% per month is added. Fraudulent export refund claims are subject to administrative penalties of up to 100% of the evaded tax, minimum fine provisions, imprisonment under Law No. 67 of 2016 and the Egyptian Penal Code, and disqualification from future VAT refund programs.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - Foreign Exchange Administration under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Banking and Banking Sector Law) and its Executive Regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt uses a market-determined flexible exchange-rate regime (restored 2024). Current-account transactions (trade, services, dividend remittances) are broadly convertible via licensed banks subject to standard documents (invoice, Bill of Lading, tax clearance). Capital-account inflows (FDI, shareholder loans, foreign-currency financing) require CBE registration and issuance of an Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) establishing the legal capital basis. Profit-remittance hurdles are practical: audited financials, e-Tax clearance, Form 41 certificate, board minutes, and IRC-linked capital-entry evidence are mandatory; interbank liquidity is the main delay point.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be repatriated to an Egyptian authorized bank within 180 days from Bill of Lading date and credited to the exporter's local account; offshore retention beyond that window is prohibited. A CBE circularic conversion and surrender ratio applies (prevailing benchmark: 50 to 100 percent of repatriated proceeds); the exporter must offer the foreign currency to the bank and may retain the unconverted balance only in a CBE-approved foreign-currency account under an approved treasury policy. Breach triggers refusal of new export documents, suspension of trade-finance lines, and enhanced CBE administrative scrutiny.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account & Operational EGP/FX Account
Capital Escrow Account & Operational EGP/FX Account
Operational EGP/FX Account (Treasury and Trade Hub)
Operational EGP/FX Account with International Correspondent Network

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for in-country treasury and clearing. Offshore electronic-money institutions (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) are not licensed banks or authorized payment-service providers under Egypt's Payment Services Law No. 18 of 2020 and cannot hold EGP or access CBE settlement systems (RTGS, ACH, Meeza). EMIs can serve only as auxiliary overseas-receivable collection and visibility tools. All CBE-regulated trade, capital, and tax flows must settle through licensed Egyptian banks; an EMI-only treasury structure is legally non-viable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for ultimate beneficial owners, legal representatives, and at least one authorized signatory at account opening, per CBE AML/CFT rules (Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended) and bank underwriting standards. Full remote onboarding is not permitted for a non-resident-owned LLC. The narrow exception uses a notarized power of attorney to Egyptian counsel plus a preliminary secure audio-video interview, followed by an in-person compliance visit within 90 days. Foreign-issued documents must be legalized or apostilled, translated into Arabic by a sworn translator, and accompanied by current commercial-register extracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership concentration and layered UBO chain creating beneficiary-opacity red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO declaration with natural-person breakdown above statutory thresholds; certified commercial-register extract; notarized LLC contract and memorandum of association; complete shareholding chain and shareholder register; passport copies, CVs, and professional references for all UBOs; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; parent-company audited financial statements where a corporate shareholder exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trade to sanctions-exposed mining and infrastructure markets, including spare-part resale or transshipment risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-level sanctions-screening matrix; end-use and end-user certificates from project owners and OEM customers; detailed product coding (HS 8431/8207) with invoice, packing list, and CIF/FOB data; customs export declarations filed through Egypt's NAFEZA and Advance Cargo Information (ACI) platforms; transportation and insurance records; signed undertaking against transshipment to embargoed parties; periodic trade-compliance attestation to the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin local balance sheet with planned foreign capital injection, triggering thin-capitalization and source-of-funds scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved capital-injection plan and treasury policy; notarized LLC contract; share subscription and premium agreements; audited opening balance sheet; signed TBM spare-part supply and project contracts evidencing future revenue; parent-company bank reference and credit opinion; CBE FDI registration forms and wire-purpose narratives.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High contractual payment velocities via commercial letters of credit and project-financing schedules triggering transaction-monitoring alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Inventory of underlying construction and infrastructure project contracts; approved counterparty whitelist; copies of LC terms, invoices, packing lists, and electronic customs clearances; treasury policy segregating EGP and FX obligations; multi-currency cash-flow model; independent audit and attestation presented to the onboarding committee.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward FDI equity and shareholder-loan proceeds must route via SWIFT MT103/MT202 through a Tier-1 correspondent bank to the LLC's account at an Egyptian authorized bank. Purpose codes follow IMF BPM6 / ISO 20022: 'Direct investment in reporting economy - equity capital', with a narrative identifying the Egyptian LLC, ISIC 2824 manufacturing activity, and CBE FDI registration. The receiving bank files the CBE inward-transfer and FDI registration, converts through the interbank market, and issues an Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) retained for future dividend remittances and liquidation. Required verification documents: notarized LLC contract, board subscription resolution, passport and source-of-funds documentation for founders, and a completed CBE declaration form.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements use: (1) SWIFT MT103/MT202 for open-account and advance-payment disbursements; (2) commercial letters of credit (sight and usance) issued or confirmed by Egyptian banks to overseas suppliers of heavy-duty sub-assemblies; (3) documentary collections (D/P and D/A) for established vendors; and (4) local EGP ACH and instant rails for domestic costs. All import shipments are subject to Egypt's Advance Cargo Information (ACI) pre-shipment registration, CBE trade-finance approval, and customs e-clearance documentation; the LLC must present a coherent invoice, LC draft, Bill of Lading, packing list, and EGP source-of-funds report per shipment, with FX purchases executed by the bank under CBE reporting requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts backed by evidenced trade or project exposure, authorized and reported by the CBE
Offshore non-deliverable EGP forwards (NDFs) for mismatch hedging via internationally integrated banks, under a documented treasury policy and CBE-compliant booking
FX cross-currency swaps (fixed/floating) for medium-term project financing and EGP/EUR/USD liquidity matching
Comprehensive currency swap structures (principal exchange) for long-term EPC and TBM spare-part contracts and commercial-LC portfolios
FX options and structured hedges, permitted only when an underlying transaction is fully evidenced and the arranging Egyptian bank holds current CBE authorizations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registration Annual Renewal (Commercial Registry Record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry of Egypt (administered within GAFI's unified registration portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1–31 January each calendar year, regardless of incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers a 50% surcharge and progressive fines under Commercial Registry Law No. 34/1976; continuous non-renewal for over 12 months can lead to suspension of the registry record and administrative strike-off of the company; carrying on business after suspension is an unregistered-activity offense.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Income Tax Card (Bitaqa Dhareebiya) Annual Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), local tax office of the legal address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal window of 1–31 January each year; card is valid through 31 December of the renewal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs a monthly administrative fine (EGP 500 in the first month) and blocks issuance of tax clearance certificates required for customs releases, bank facilities and public tenders; prolonged default risks administrative closure of the business premises.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Register Confirmation via e-UBO Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Beneficial Ownership e-portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January, aligned with the commercial registry renewal; event-driven UBO updates due within 30 days of any share transfer or change of ultimate control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or to maintain an accurate UBO register is punishable under AML Law No. 80/2002 by a fine of EGP 20,000–EGP 100,000; willful concealment of beneficial owners may also lead to imprisonment and exclusion from public procurement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Annual Return with Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Final return and settlement within 4 months after fiscal year-end (30 April for calendar-year companies); ETA-issued provisional advance CIT assessments are payable during the fiscal year per the current ETA schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues a monthly penalty of 2% of the unpaid tax under Article 121 of Income Tax Law No. 91/2005; failure to file subjects the company to ETA default assessment, administrative fines and criminal liability of the responsible managers for deliberate non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Assembly (AGA) Approval of Audited Financial Statements and Reappointment of Financial Controller/Auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ordinary General Assembly of shareholders; certified minutes recorded in the statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Meeting must be convened within 6 months of fiscal year-end (30 June for calendar-year companies), subject to the maximum extension permitted by the Articles of Association
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Managers who fail to convene the annual general assembly within the statutory deadline are liable to administrative fines under Companies Law No. 194/2020; failure to approve audited accounts blocks dividend distributions and GAFI annual clearance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Payroll Reconciliation and Social Insurance Wage Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly contribution declarations and payments due by the 15th of the following month; annual aggregate payroll and wage declaration due 31 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delayed payment incurs an additional monthly charge of 2% of unpaid contributions under Unified Social Insurance Law No. 148/2019; NISO may initiate executive attachment against the company's bank accounts and employer sanction proceedings for arrears.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Withholding Tax (WHT) Reconciliation and Non-Resident Payments Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly WHT returns due by the 15th of the month following the deduction; annual reconciliation filed with the CIT annual return no later than 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unreported or underpaid withholding tax carries the 2% monthly late-payment penalty; the company as withholding agent remains jointly liable for the full tax amount plus fines on payments made to non-resident suppliers without proper deduction.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Egyptian law provides a general corporate income tax rate of 22.5% for commercial and industrial activities. No general statutory tax holiday is available for standard manufacturing, but a 10% reduced rate applies to certain export-oriented or labor-intensive activities in specified governorates. For companies operating in the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) or under the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, incentives are granted through capital cost deductions (up to 50% of investment costs for specified activities) and possible customs exemptions, not a blanket income tax holiday. Investment Law incentives may cap the applicable rate at the statutory rate, but treated as deductions to taxable basis. Accordingly, the effective tax rate is typically 22.5% unless qualifying for a reduced 10% rate or investment cost deduction mechanisms.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian Corporate Income Tax Return Form No. 114 (Bayan al-Dakhl al-Khass) filed through the Egyptian Tax Authority's (ETA) online e-filing portal (www.eta.gov.eg) or the unified 'Erada' / 'Tax Automation' system for companies registered in the Large Taxpayer Office (LTO) or SCZONE administrative window.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual CIT return must be filed within 4 months from the end of the fiscal year (i.e. by 31 May for a 31 December year-end). For companies with approved non-calendar fiscal years, the due date is within 4 months of the fiscal year-end. Provisional quarterly tax declarations and payments are due within 30 days of the end of each quarter (substantive tax prepayments based on previous year's taxable income).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification details: Company legal name, tax card number, tax file number, commercial registration number, address of the Egyptian head office or registered branch, and e-mail address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident LLC shareholders acting as filings for the Egyptian entity must insert the Egyptian tax ID and permanent establishment (PE) registration code if the LLC is deemed to have a PE; otherwise, the form must be submitted by the resident legal representative. No non-resident foreign address should be placed in the box without an appointed Egyptian tax representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period and financial statement basis (start date, end date, currency used, method of accounting cash vs. accrual, and books retention compliance).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an LLC owned by non-residents, the accounting period must align with the audited Egyptian financial statements; IFRS or Egyptian Financial Reporting Standards (EFRS) are accepted, and foreign parent consolidation schedules should be attached as supplementary disclosures only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of net taxable profit: net accounting profit before tax per the audited income statement, followed by adjustments for disallowable expenses, exempt income, depreciation, provisions, and tax loss carryforward deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders should ensure that all intercompany charges (management fees, royalties, interest) deducted in Box 3 are backed by transfer pricing documentation and are not non-deductible 'undisclosed expenses'; otherwise the local tax inspector will add back those amounts as deemed dividends or disallowed expenditure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of depreciable fixed assets: historical cost, accumulated depreciation, tax depreciation rates applied, and addition/deletion during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: TBM spare-parts manufacturers importing heavy equipment must ensure depreciation is computed on the invoiced customs value and that any tax depreciation rate exceeding the ETA-published industrial machinery rate (commonly 10%-15% on a straight-line basis) creates a temporary difference requiring deferred tax accounting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of provisions and reserves: book provisions (doubtful debts, warranties, inventories) and the amount added back as a taxable reserve unless actually paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign-owned LLC, provisions for contingent liabilities under IFRS are typically non-deductible until realized; hence the field must reflect an add-back to avoid under-ascertainment of taxable income and associated penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of exempt income and tax-free investment returns: dividends received from Egyptian joint-stock companies, treasury bill margins, and SCZONE investment incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent shareholders must not claim exemption for upstream dividends remitted by the Egyptian LLC unless the dividend-sourcing rules are satisfied. The LLC itself can only exclude Egyptian-dividend income if the participation exceeds a 25% threshold and the payer is subject to tax in Egypt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of foreign tax credits: taxes paid abroad on income also taxed in Egypt, including the underlying tax treatment and relevant DTA article.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a non-resident parent has a foreign branch income pass-through arrangement or the Egyptian LLC derives income from a PE abroad, the LLC may claim a unilateral credit of up to the Egyptian tax attributable to that foreign income, subject to a double-tax treaty cap and presentation of foreign tax assessments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing declaration and controlled transaction summary: aggregate value of transactions with related parties, the method used (CUP, resale, cost-plus, TNMM), and compliance statement under Art. 57 bis of Law No. 91 of 2005.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent companies must attach the statutory Transfer Pricing Form (attached to the CIT return) listing the global entity, Egyptian LLC, the nature of cross-border payments, the intercompany agreement reference, and the selected pricing method. Failing to attach the schedule renders the return formally deficient.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income and final tax computation: application of 22.5% headline rate, offset of tax payments, and resulting balance payable or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian LLC should compute the final tax on an entity-level basis; non-resident investors cannot consolidate the LLC's losses or profits with their own income in Egypt other than through a PE

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is 2% of the tax due per month or part thereof, capped at 50% of the aggregate tax due. Late payment penalty is 1.5% per month of the unpaid tax amount. If the return is knowingly false or incomplete to evade tax, an additional penalty of up to 40% of the tax difference can be imposed. For failure to file despite notice, the ETA may assess the tax ex officio on the basis of available evidence and impose triple tax (treble assessment) in cases of proven tax evasion. Directors and the resident manager are jointly liable for such penalties to the extent of the LLC's unpaid tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions of profits by Egyptian LLCs to tax-resident shareholders; for non-resident shareholders, Egyptian domestic law historically treats dividends as exempt from withholding when paid from a company whose profits are subject to Egyptian corporate tax. There is no separate statutory dividend withholding tax on distributions made by an Egyptian company to non-resident shareholders under Law No. 91 of 2005, provided the profits have borne the 22.5% CIT. Consequently, no WHT is applied to a dividend distribution from an Egyptian LLC. This is subject to anti-abuse rules where the distribution is disguised as an excessive interest, royalty, or service fee payment, in which case the payment is recharacterized and 20% withholding applies at source on treaty-covered or non-treaty income.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because Egypt does not impose a statutory dividend withholding tax on profits already subject to CIT, non-resident shareholders do not need a double-tax treaty relief application solely to reduce dividend WHT. However, when the ETA recharacterizes a cross-border payment (interest/royalties/management fees) as a dividend because of thin capitalization or substance failure, the taxpayer must invoke the applicable DTA (e.g. Egypt-UAE, Egypt-UK, Egypt-Germany, Egypt-China) by submitting the following: (1) a completed Bireau de Renseignements / Competent Authority Relief Request via the ETA International Taxation Department; (2) an Egyptian Tax Residency Certificate of the receiving foreign company; (3) a foreign tax residency certificate (Form 6166 for US, or equivalent for other jurisdictions) duly apostilled/legalized; (4) beneficial ownership declaration and the underlying contract (loan, license, service contract); (5) the LLC's audited financial statements and evidence that the cross-border payee has substance. Treaty relief is typically granted through the reduced withholding rate at source, or via a refund claim within 5 years of the end of the calendar year in which tax was withheld. The ETA generally requires the treaty relief application to be filed before payment or at the time of the annual CIT return, and the foreign payee must hold a valid Egyptian tax ID or a dedicated treaty-access code for refund procedures.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory domestic rate: 20% on interest, royalties, annuities, and consideration for technical or administrative services paid to non-resident persons without a PE in Egypt. No domestic withholding on dividends as stated above. Treaty-reduced rates commonly applied: interest 10% (Egypt-UAE, Egypt-Qatar, Egypt-Kuwait, Egypt-China, Egypt-UK, Egypt-Germany treaties), royalties 5%-10% depending on treaty and type of intellectual property (e.g. Egypt-UK applies 10%, Egypt-China 8%, Egypt-UAE 0% in certain licensing of industrial equipment? No — precise: Egypt-UAE royalty WHT is 5%; Egypt-Germany is 10%; Egypt-France is 10%; Egypt-Netherlands is 10%. In all cases, the beneficial owner must not merely be a conduit and the Egyptian LLC must not deduct the payment unless the WHT has been settled with a receipt (Form 50 or bank receipt).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The Egyptian TP Documentation thresholds under Ministerial Decree No. 524 of 2018 and subsequent amendments require a Local File and Master File where the related-party transactions per class exceed EGP 10 million annually (by aggregate category) or EGP 2 million for transactions with persons resident in a zero-tax jurisdiction. The previously proposed thresholds of EGP 5 million were superseded by EGP 10 million per transaction category. The Egyptian LLC in the heavy TBM spare-parts sector must prepare and retain contemporaneous documentation if the aggregate value of cross-border purchases from the foreign parent or affiliates exceeds EGP 10 million per annum, or if loans/royalties to related parties exceed EGP 2 million. Loss-making entities with intercompany revenue below materiality thresholds may still be notified by the ETA; functional, risk, and economic substance analyses must be prepared on a best-practice basis regardless of formal threshold.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt has currently issued draft/framework Economic Substance Regulations as of 2023-2024, but has not enacted a comprehensive ESR statute comparable to UAE or Bahrain. The applicable substantive test arises through general anti-avoidance principles in Law No. 91 of 2005, Law No. 82 of 2020 (Tax Evasion Combating Law), and ministerial tax inspections. The ETA can disregard an Egyptian LLC entirely if the company is a shell or lacks physical presence, employees, premises, or real business conduct, and recharacterize revenue as income of the foreign principal. Despite no formal ESR registration system in Egypt, multinational groups must demonstrate the Egyptian LLC has decision-making capacity, procurement and inventory management functions, engineering staff, and operational substance in EG/SCZONE; otherwise transfer pricing adjustments and deemed distributions can be made with double-tax consequences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LLC deliberately omits gross sales from the CIT return, fabricates purchase invoices for imported TBM spare parts, or uses falsified export documents to claim an export tax exemption or reduced effective tax rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law No. 91 of 2005 and Law No. 82 of 2020, tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment of not less than 6 months and a fine equal to 3 to 10 times the tax evaded; in severe repeated cases the fine reaches up to 10 times the avoided tax plus closure of the establishment. The ETA additionally levies an ex officio assessment with penalties of 2% per month (late payment penalty) and an additional 40% of the difference for misstatement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The resident manager and all directors who signed the return or who controlled the business are jointly and severally liable for the entirety of the tax difference and penalties. In criminal cases, the court may impose travel bans, asset freezing measures, and imprisonment for up to 5 years for executives with actual knowledge and intent. Civil restitution orders allow attachment of the personal assets of directors if the LLC is insolvent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Artificial Substance Arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Egyptian LLC is used as a passive holding invoice vehicle with no physical office in Egypt/SCZONE, no employees or operational management, and the entire order-taking, negotiation, engineering, and delivery decisions are made by the foreign parent. It merely bills contracts at a zero spread or recognizes artificial losses on intercompany inventory purchases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA or SCZONE authority invokes anti-abuse rules and disregards the LLC for tax purposes. The invoice route is treated as a sham, and taxable revenue is reallocated to the foreign principal's Egyptian PE or to the local party, resulting in a 22.5% tax on the gross recharacterized margin plus an additional 40% penalty for deliberate misrepresentation and up to EGP 2 million administrative fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the foreign parent who knowingly used the Egyptian shell as a fiction can be named in criminal prosecutions under the anti-money laundering framework, with penalties including 3 to 7 years' imprisonment and a fine of EGP 100,000 to EGP 1,000,000. The Egyptian nominee director is personally liable for the LLC's unpaid tax and may face a travel ban and passport seizure pending settlement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mismatch and Thin Capitalization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LLC pays royalties and management fees at 20% above the arm's length range to the foreign parent while maintaining an EGP-denominated intercompany loan with no interest or with interest exceeding the Egyptian prime rate; the LLC fails to attach TP disclosure Form and has no contemporaneous documentation, and the net profit is artificially zero.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA performs a TP adjustment, disallows the excess royalties/fees, applies the general 22.5% tax rate on the upward adjustment, adds late payment interest of 1.5% per month, and imposes a misstatement penalty of 40% of the total additional tax due. If the intercompany loan is recharacterized as equity, the interest paid is treated as a constructive dividend and subject to 0% WHT, but the interest non-deduction is confirmed and the tax base is enlarged.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The foreign-appointed director and the CFO are jointly liable for the additional tax if they prepared or approved the inaccurate return and documented false invoices. The directors may be subject to a personal fine in criminal prosecution equal to the difference between the tax assessed and the tax paid, plus imprisonment of up to 2 years if the ETA proves deliberate fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Economic Sanctions Compliance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The export of underground TBM spare parts is routed through a high-risk jurisdiction (or brokered by a sanctioned entity), or the LLC receives contract proceeds from a project-financing scheme through an unlicensed foreign bank account outside the Egyptian banking system and fails to file the cross-border transaction declaration or beneficial ownership statement under AML Law No. 80 of 2002.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) may impose a fine of EGP 50,000 to EGP 300,000 per violation on the LLC, and the ETA assesses tax on the non-declared cash inflow at 22.5% with a penalty of 2% per month. In aggravated cases, the account is frozen and the LLC is blacklisted from government procurement and SCZONE licences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board directors and the compliance officer may be prosecuted for AML facilitation; imprisonment ranges from 2 to 7 years for knowing concealment of illicit funds. The court may freeze the personal accounts of directors, order confiscation of an equivalent value, and impose travel bans pending full recovery and settlement of the tax liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LLC imports steel castings or grinding parts from the parent/affiliates at artificially low values in the customs invoice to reduce customs duty, thereby decreasing the cost base and distorting the tax return; or overstates the customs value to inflate deductible depreciation and obtain foreign exchange conversion concessions for spare-parts imports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Egyptian Customs Law No. 207 of 2020, under-declaration of customs value is punishable by a fine of 20% to 40% of the customs duties evaded and forfeiture/conversion of the goods; the ETA recalculates taxable income using the arm's length price and unjustified depreciation adjustments, leading to an additional assessment of the tax difference plus 40% penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The company's import director and the legal representative are jointly and severally liable for customs debts. Customs authorities can issue an executive seizure order against personal assets, and administrative imprisonment (up to 90 days) may be imposed until the duties are paid. If the under-invoicing is linked to FX-related money laundering, imprisonment can extend to 5 years.
